title: Blend two colors into a gradient

seo.metaTitle: Blend Two Colors PNG - Free Gradient Maker, No Upload
seo.metaDescription: Blend two colors into one continuous horizontal gradient PNG. Set the pair and the width, then download as PNG, JPG, WebP or BMP. Free, nothing is uploaded.
seo.longDescription: Blend two colors draws every step of the path between them as a single continuous horizontal strip: the first color at the left edge, the second at the right edge, and every pixel in between carrying its own mix of the two. Use it to see how a background fade will really look before writing the CSS, to preview a hover transition, or to sample the middle tone of a two-color scheme. There is no source file — the blend is computed per pixel on your device. The strip is always horizontal, its height is a quarter of its width, and there is no angle control; for a diagonal or any exact size use the linear gradient tool.
facts: Computed entirely in your browser: no upload, no server, no signup.
Width from 128 to 1024 px; the height follows at a quarter of it.
Always horizontal, no angle — the linear gradient tool adds both.
Per-pixel floating-point blend; faint banding is possible only on very low contrast pairs.
Free with no daily limit, no watermark and no account, also for commercial use.
howTo: No upload needed - this tool draws the strip from the two colors you pick.
Set the Color pair: the first color lands on the left edge, the second on the right.
Set the Width between 128 and 1024 pixels; the height follows at a quarter of it.
Download the blend as PNG, JPG, WebP or BMP from the Download button.

faq.q: What is the difference between this and the linear gradient tool?
faq.a: This one is deliberately minimal: two colors, a width, always horizontal. The linear gradient tool adds an angle and lets you set any canvas size, which is what you want for a diagonal fade or an exact hero section size.

faq.q: Can I get the intermediate colors as separate swatches?
faq.a: Not here, because the blend is continuous. Use the color steps tool to get a discrete, evenly spaced set of the same two colors, or the monochromatic tool to build a tone ramp from a single base.

faq.q: Why does the strip look like it has visible bands?
faq.a: The blend is computed in floating point and rounded to whole bytes, so a very wide, very low contrast pair can still show faint steps once it is quantized. Raise the contrast between the two colors and the banding disappears.

faq.q: Do I need an account or to upload anything?
faq.a: No. There is no signup, no watermark and no daily limit, and no file is ever sent anywhere - the strip is built in your browser and the tool is open source.
